newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares extend two year high.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares extend two year high.

text.p: Egyptian share prices extended a two-year high on Wednesday with cement, mills and some housing stocks clocking up gains.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index added 3.95 points to 248.43, its highest level since mid-November 1994. Turnover was an average 35.50 million pounds ($10.44 million).
"It's rising, rising, rising," said one broker. "Mills and the cement sector are going up."
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was the best performer, rising almost 31 percent to close at 250.30 pounds. It also had the day's highest turnover of 7.5 million.
Heliopolis Housing and Development rose 13.5 percent to close at 210.00 pounds, the second highest gainer of the day.
Mills shares put in a good showing.

North Cairo Flour Mills shares rose 3.50 pounds to end at 120.50 while more than 3.2 million pounds changed hands. Central and West Delta Flour Mills rose ten percent to close at 68.31 pounds. Another top mills performer was Upper Egypt Flour Mills which gained 0.81, closing at 52.15.
Suez Cement was prominent again, with a 1.52 pound gain to 52.52. It had the third highest turnover of the day with 2.01 million worth of shares changing hands.
The company's performance has been attributed to an apparent anticipation of the global depositary receipt (GDR) offering which Salomon Brothers is arranging.

National Bank of Egypt (NBE) chairman Mahmoud Abdelaziz told Reuters last week all the details of the GDR should be announced by the end of this month. NBE is one of the public-sector banks selling some of its Suez Cement shares.
Egyptian Portland Tora Cement slipped 0.90 pounds to close at 67.00 pounds in 1.64 million pounds turnover.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 370.36 from 365.51 points on Tuesday, and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 175.6 from 172.53.
